root_cause_detail: fraud-scoring-eu is timing out for 38% of calls in eu-west-1 (confirmed on the provider status page). checkout-web blocks on that call, retries twice and converts the 8s provider latency into 504s for customers. No deploy, no pool saturation, no internal saturation: every internal dependency is healthy.
resolution: Enabled degraded mode: skip synchronous fraud scoring, flag orders for asynchronous review, and keep the circuit breaker open for the provider. Checkout p95 fell to 610ms. A provider-side status update closed the incident 34 minutes later.
resolution_summary: Degraded mode + circuit breaker (no code change)
contributing_factors: Fraud scoring is called synchronously on the confirmation path with no timeout budget or fallback
Two retries of an 8s call add 16s of worst-case latency per checkout
The circuit breaker was half-open rather than fully open, so retries kept hammering a failing provider
No provider health was on the checkout dashboard, so responders first suspected their own deploys
prevention: Make fraud scoring asynchronous by default with a hard 1.2s budget
Fully open the circuit breaker after 20% timeout rate instead of half-opening
Put third-party provider health on the checkout dashboard
Add a synthetic checkout that runs without the provider
runbook_changes: Add a first branch: 'is an external provider degraded? check the dependency graph before touching code'
Document the degraded-mode switch and who may enable it
Explicitly note that a deploy older than 72h is not a correlate
lessons: An external dependency can produce a latency incident that looks like an application fault; the dependency graph decides it in seconds.
Restarting checkout-web did not help at all - restarting an application cannot fix a provider outage.
Rolling back a release deployed three days ago was a wasted 12 minutes and would have been pure superstition; deploy correlation has a time window.
Degraded mode is the correct mitigation when the fault is outside your control: trade a manual review queue for restored checkout.
first_checks: dependency graph: which downstream is unhealthy
provider timeout rate and the provider status page
is there any deploy inside the correlation window (last 60 minutes)
is the circuit breaker open for the failing provider
confirmed_by: checkout confirm p95 below 1s and 504 rate at baseline while the provider is bypassed
memory_episode: INC-C1 (checkout-web, SEV-2): checkout confirm p95 8.1s and 504s because fraud-scoring-eu timed out on 38% of calls (provider partial outage). No deploy inside the window; redis and postgres healthy. Resolved by enabling degraded mode (skip synchronous fraud scoring, async review) plus a fully open circuit breaker. Check first next time: the dependency graph and provider timeout rate, not your own deploys.
memory_service_pattern: checkout-web depends on the external provider fraud-scoring-eu synchronously on the checkout confirmation path. Its characteristic failure is a provider partial outage showing as 504s and ~8s latency with healthy internal dependencies. The correct mitigation is degraded mode; restarts and rollbacks do nothing.
